title: Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity
answer: Authorship, hallucination and fact checking, training data provenance, ethics review and provenance of research images and data.

children.name: AI and Authorship
children.blurb: AI and authorship concerns who or what can be credited as an author when artificial intelligence contributes to research writing, data analysis, or idea generation.

children.name: Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking
children.blurb: Fabricated citations and fact checking concern the detection, documentation, and prevention of references that do not correspond to real published work, and the verification of claims made in AI research papers.

children.name: Training Data and Academic Work
children.blurb: This topic covers the use of scholarly texts, including journal articles, preprints, theses, textbooks and course materials, as training data for machine learning systems.

children.name: Ethics Review with AI Assistance
children.blurb: AI assistance in ethics review means using machine learning tools to help research ethics committees and institutional review boards screen protocols, identify risks, check consent forms, and flag missing safeguards.

children.name: Provenance of Research Images and Data
children.blurb: Provenance of research images and data concerns the documented origin, processing history, and chain of custody for visual and tabular evidence used in scientific work.

sections.body: This section covers the practical work of keeping AI research honest. It looks at who gets credit when an AI helps write a paper, how false citations and invented facts are caught, where training data comes from, how ethics boards use AI tools, and how images and datasets are traced back to their source. The work is not theoretical. Researchers now use automated tools to compare reference lists against databases, flag passages that look generated, and log the origin of every image file in a study. AI is also being used to scan grant applications and manuscripts for signs of image duplication or missing ethics approvals.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Detecting a made up citation is fairly reliable when the cited paper does not exist, but catching a real paper used to support a false claim is much harder. Authorship tools can estimate how much of a text was machine written, yet they produce false positives and cannot prove intent. Training data provenance is improving for large public datasets, but many academic models are released without a full list of their sources. Ethics review with AI assistance can speed up routine checks, but it cannot replace human judgment about harm to participants. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,555 extracted claims shows how much material must be checked, but the checking itself remains incomplete and error prone.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader worried about credit should start with AI and Authorship, which explains how journals and universities are deciding when a machine counts as a contributor. Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking then covers the tools that catch fake references and the limits of those tools. Training Data and Academic Work connects to both, because a model trained on flawed or unlicensed text is more likely to produce bad citations and unclear authorship. Ethics Review with AI Assistance shows how review boards use software to screen proposals, while Provenance of Research Images and Data follows the trail of evidence after a study is published. Together these pages move from who wrote the work, to whether its sources are real, to where its data came from, to how it was approved, and finally to whether its images can be trusted.
